content: Keeps the company reckoning book and holds the stock share
Collects the £20 Greenwich court warrant on 15 March
Their pay is as slow as ours, and he will say so and stop.
He will not strike a share, and he will not give a figure the cloth does not hold.
He will not unwrite a book to oblige a parlour, and he will not invent a sum the box does not yet hold.
He will set a week without putting a share, a coffer, or a part on the leaf.
He counts the ladies before he counts the poetry, and he can say a gown in the same breath as a boy's sleeves without buying either.
He will want four afternoons, name two days, and refuse a jig without raising his voice. The Mayor next door is his best argument.
He will name a mercer's figure from the shop, and he will not invent one in a yard he has not stood in.
He will name a share exactly, and he will not let it pay a different debt.
He asks for a Love's Labour's Won half in jest, and he does not enter a trial, or an unpaid bill, as if it were cash in hand.
He will not give a week a figure the book has not taught him, and he will not lend it last week's thirty.
He will touch the table once for a winter without a purse-quarrel, and he will not write fellowship down as a loss.
On Saturday he kept the stock's share of the twenty pound after Kemp objected to an eighth part, and he said the seven yards of peach velvet wait until autumn.
He paid Edith eight shillings out of the stock and said that a debt paid by the stock is not a man drawing his share.
He counts the days out loud, and he keeps a boy's if off the boy's ears.
A share of thirty-eight shillings does not open the coffer, and twice does not oblige the company twice unless someone agrees.
He will say a share and he will not say a total.
Forty shillings, said once. Last Saturday was eight-and-twenty. The sheet is the share, and the lease is a different paper. The chest is not counted.
A glass is four shillings, and it will be broken every time. He does not name a Rose sum he has not got.
He will not name a share while the bag is open, and he will not supply a sum he has not got.
He will take a comedy he already has, ask for a second in the same breath, and shut the almanac on a map that still has no sum in it.
He would rather play a thin yard than have the Mayor write that the company feared its own audience.
He will still not set a figure on a thin afternoon, and he will not borrow one.
His man took the canvas. Nothing came back. Bankside, he said, has nowhere else of an afternoon.
He would have the old comedies and the peace written down, and he set the July roads with no answer.
He will hear a dangerous page, and he will still ask where the week is written down as a week you may play it.
He will say a figure once, propose the five pound in the same call, and wait to be told to pay it.
He asks on what, and he writes the answer down as a going, not as a debate.
He tells a share as a count on the cloth, and he names the next day's bill in the same breath.
He prices the gilt at four shillings and the hem at eighteenpence, and he can hear a thick voice from a call.
Thirty-four stands on the line, and he does not want the coffer.
He will say a wage, a Thursday box, and a share in one reckoning, and he will not divide them when the division would invent a third figure.
He will say thirty-eight, and last week's forty-five, and he will not invent a tale to explain the difference. The hired men's ten stays where Saturday last left it.
He stops at the foot of the stair, leaves the roll with Pope, and will not invent the length of a cut cue.
He will say the hard sentence twice, and he will shut the book on a question rather than on a sum.
He stated thirty-five shillings as a share and left Christmas with no date and no sum.
He will guess a country justice and stop, and he will not read a receipt he has not got.
He will count a share by candle and he will not turn it into a coffer.
He pays for a clean licence, and he will not open a cut to soothe a slight.
He takes a joy by the item. A company eleven pound richer of a Thursday is his item, and it is not a line in the book.
He will say a box and a share in the same breath and refuse to divide them when the arithmetic will not bear it.
He will not rule a week the court has not played, and he will not say a deposit twice.
He will not make a share out of four shillings and tenpence, and he will not enter a likeness as if it had been paid.
He keeps my lord's purse on one leaf and the Queen's three nights on another, and he will not be teased into joining them.
